Chapter 12 — The Call to Mission: Living Out Faith in the World.
You know, faith isn’t something we’re meant to keep hidden away or locked inside. If you’ve ever read *The Valley of Vision*, you’ll notice how many of the prayers look outward—urging us to live with purpose, and to actually make a difference in the world around us. They remind us that devotion isn’t just about our own personal growth, but about loving and serving others, too.
Imagine feeling that tug—maybe you’re thinking about reaching out to a neighbor, volunteering your time, or speaking up for what’s right. That desire to help is there, but so are the doubts. You might wonder, “What if I fail? What if I’m not enough?” The prayers in this chapter give voice to those questions. They ask for courage, for wisdom, and for a heart that’s willing to take action, even when it’s scary.
There’s a real sense of urgency and compassion in these prayers. They’re all about asking for eyes that notice the needs around us, and hands that are ready to help. And underneath it all, there’s a longing—a longing to be part of something bigger, to actually make an impact. But there’s also a deep humility here. These prayers ask for the strength to serve without needing credit, and to love without expecting anything back.
And here’s something important: Mission, as it’s described in these prayers, isn’t about making grand gestures or doing something heroic. It’s about being faithful in the little things. Maybe it’s showing kindness to someone who’s struggling, speaking the truth when it matters, or just living each day with integrity. The message is clear—every single one of us has a role to play, and even the smallest act of love can create a ripple that spreads far beyond what we see.
If you ever feel overwhelmed by all the needs in the world, these prayers offer some much-needed perspective. They remind us that real change starts with just one step, and that no effort—no matter how small—is ever wasted. *The Valley of Vision* encourages us to live outward-focused lives, marked by generosity, compassion, and the courage to act.
